court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma

issues.label: Standard for above-guidelines income support
issues.why: Father's income exceeds the $15,000 maximum, requiring the court to determine support beyond the guideline schedule.

issues.label: Best interests and children's actual needs
issues.why: Above-guideline support must be based on the children's demonstrated needs and best interests rather than an arbitrary figure.

issues.label: Basing support on Father's volunteered offer
issues.why: The court set support at $2,250 solely because Father offered it, which may not be a proper evidentiary or legal basis.

issues.label: Refusal to follow Archer v. Archer
issues.why: The court expressly declined to follow controlling precedent, and its authority to depart must be assessed.

issues.label: Weight of evidence on children's expenses
issues.why: Mother presented detailed expense evidence while Father lacked personal knowledge, implicating the clearly-against-weight standard.

issues.label: Father's credibility and lack of knowledge
issues.why: Father had seen the children once in three years and provided no calculation, affecting reliability of his expense estimate.

issues.label: Abuse of discretion review of support
issues.why: The support order stands unless clearly against the weight of the evidence constituting abuse of discretion.

issues.label: De novo review of legal questions
issues.why: Underlying legal issues, such as interpreting guidelines for high income, are reviewed de novo.

issues.label: Effect of Father's notice violation
issues.why: Father failed to give the required 25% income-change notice, which may bear on retroactivity and equities.

issues.label: Retroactive modification effective date
issues.why: Support modification may be effective from the motion's filing given Father's non-notice and income increases.

issues.label: Statutory authority for attorney fees
issues.why: Fees require a specific statute or agreement, so the court must identify a valid basis for any award.

issues.label: Ability to pay in fee award
issues.why: Relative financial resources and Father's greater ability to pay are relevant to fee allocation.

issues.label: Limiting fees to discovery efforts
issues.why: The court awarded only discovery-related fees without explaining exclusion of other reasonable fees.

issues.label: Adequacy of court's fee findings
issues.why: The court failed to elaborate reasons for denying non-discovery fees, raising sufficiency-of-explanation concerns.

issues.label: Father's litigation conduct and delays
issues.why: Father's attorney changes and discovery delays may justify a broader fee award as sanctionable conduct.

issues.label: Effect of Mother's declined settlement offers
issues.why: Father argues Mother's refusal to settle should reduce fees, requiring evaluation of that equitable factor.

issues.label: Mother's earning capacity argument
issues.why: Father contends Mother could earn more as a lawyer, implicating imputed income considerations.

issues.label: Reasonableness of fee amount
issues.why: The court found the requested amount reasonable, but must justify awarding only a portion.

issues.label: Registration of foreign paternity decree jurisdiction
issues.why: Support modification authority depends on proper registration and continuing jurisdiction over the Texas decree.

issues.label: Enforceability of 2021 order's self-executing provisions
issues.why: The order's automatic recalculation and notice provisions affect procedure and modification obligations.
